title: SensitiveHUE: Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection by Enhancing the Sensitivity to Normal Patterns

problem.claim: Unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series must distinguish normal from abnormal points.

gap.claim: Existing reconstruction methods may be insensitive to spatio-temporal dependencies and fail to model heteroscedastic uncertainty, which can impair discrimination between normal and abnormal points.

contributions.claim: SensitiveHUE is a probabilistic network combining reconstruction with heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation.
The method uses statistical feature removal to support dependency sensitivity and an MTS-NLL loss to model normal patterns in important regions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the MTS-NLL loss as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SensitiveHUE has nontrivial sensitivity to normal patterns.
The authors report that SensitiveHUE outperforms existing state-of-the-art alternatives by a large margin.
The authors report that code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multivariate time series anomaly detection is challenging, and reconstruction-based modeling has received substantial attention.
Insensitivity to normal patterns, limited sensitivity to spatio-temporal dependencies, and missing heteroscedastic uncertainty modeling limit anomaly discrimination.
Greater sensitivity to normal patterns is presented as necessary for improving discrimination between normal and abnormal points.
SensitiveHUE combines probabilistic reconstruction and heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation with statistical feature removal and an MTS-NLL loss.
The authors report favorable experimental results and public code availability.

source_observation.claim: High noise in normal data may produce excessively high reconstruction errors and cause detection failure.

interpretation.claim: Anomaly detection criteria should account for uncertainty in normal observations rather than relying only on reconstruction error.

application.claim: For noisy multivariate time series, consider combining reconstruction with heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which noise regimes, datasets, or deployment settings support this application.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The abstract does not quantify the reported performance margin.
The implementation details of statistical feature removal and MTS-NLL are unspecified.
